citation: J. A. S. Smith, M. Blanz, T. J. Rayner, M. D. Rowe, S. Bedford, and K. Althoefer, Journal of Magnetic Resonance 213, 98-106 (2011)
title: 14N quadrupole resonance and 1H T1 dispersion in the explosive RDX
source: Publisher-hosted large figure images for Figures 2 and 8

nqr_fixture.curve: representative filled-square nu+ line near 5192 kHz
nqr_fixture.fit_regime: activated high-temperature branch before the low-temperature plateau

nmr_fixture.axis_calibration: Figure 2 log10(T1/ms) versus proton NMR frequency

sample_warning: The NMR sample was RDX in Galden oil; the NQR sample was PE4 containing approximately 88% RDX. Absolute amplitudes must not be jointly fitted without accounting for preparation.
limitations: Values are digitized from plotted symbols and are not author-supplied tables.
The NQR fixture represents one of six nearly coincident ring-nitrogen curves rather than every plotted point.
A log-linear Arrhenius fit is restricted to the activated NQR branch; it is not a replacement for the full NMR cross-relaxation dispersion model.
The paper reports no uncertainty for the approximately 92 kJ/mol activation energy in its abstract.
